newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire army pledges to fight as long as ordered to.
newsitem.headline: Zaire army pledges to fight as long as ordered to.

text.p: Zaire's armed forces chief of staff said on Wednesday that the army was fighting a war imposed on it but would fight on until ordered to do otherwise.
At the same time, General Mahele Lieko Bokoungo urged the government to take care of soldiers needs and leave the army to make its own logistics arrangements.

"The Zairean Armed Forces (FAZ), engaged in a war which is imposed on them, will continue with it until receiving contrary orders," he said in a statement read by a fellow officer at a news conference.
Mahele, appointed by Zaire's ailing President Mobutu Sese Seko in December, went on to urge his notoriously ill-disciplined soldiers to refrain from looting.
Army looting at regular intervals during Mobutu's three decades in power has alientated local Zaireans and now works in favour of rebels advancing in the east and south.
"You, those in power, take care of the fate of our soldiers," Mahele's statement said.
"He demanded that the acquisition and management of logistics of the armed forces should henceforth be the responsibility of the army," it added.
Mahele's remarks were the first since a January 20 army counter-offensive flopped in the face of rebels advances on several fronts.
